usage_en: Compliment someone by saying their skill has improved a lot. Just place a noun before 많이 늘었어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 한국어가 많이 늘었어요! 대단해요. (Your Korean has improved so much! Amazing.) or 요리 실력이 많이 늘었어요. (Your cooking skills have improved a lot.).

examples.en: Your Korean has improved so much! Amazing.
Your cooking skills have improved a lot.
You've improved a lot in just 6 months.

usage_en: Ask what someone's secret or key to success is. Say what you need, then add 비결이 뭐예요 at the end. Common uses: 피부가 너무 좋아요. 비결이 뭐예요? (Your skin looks amazing. What's your secret?) or 한국어 실력이 좋은 비결이 뭐예요? (What's the secret to your great Korean skills?).

examples.en: Your skin looks amazing. What's your secret?
What's the secret to your great Korean skills?
You always look happy. What's your secret?
examples.ko: 항상 기분이 좋아 보여요. 비결이 뭐예요?

literal_en: Formal and informal speech are still confusing to ~
usage_en: Say that something is confusing or hard to tell apart. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 존댓말이랑 반말이 아직 헷갈려요. (Formal and informal speech are still confusing to me.) or 이 두 단어 의미가 헷갈려요. (The meaning of these two words is confusing me.).

examples.en: Formal and informal speech are still confusing to me.
The meaning of these two words is confusing me.
I'm confused about the direction. Can you show me the map?
examples.ko: 방향이 헷갈려요. 지도 보여줄 수 있어요?

literal_en: Is samgyeopsal this delicious? It's seriously ~
usage_en: Express surprise that something has a quality to such a degree. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 삼겹살이 이렇게 맛있어? 진짜 대박이야. (Is samgyeopsal this delicious? It's seriously amazing.) or 한국이 이렇게 추워? 몰랐어. (Is Korea this cold? I had no idea.).

examples.en: Is samgyeopsal this delicious? It's seriously amazing.
Is Korea this cold? I had no idea.
Is this movie this fun? I want to watch it right now.
examples.ko: 이 영화가 이렇게 재밌어? 빨리 보고 싶어.

usage_en: Say a specific moment is your favorite or the best part. Say what you need, then add 이때가 제일 좋아 at the end. Common uses: 여행 중에 이때가 제일 좋아. 다 같이 밥 먹는 시간. (This is my favorite moment on the trip — eating together.) or 하루 중에 이때가 제일 좋아. 커피 마시는 아침. (This is my favorite time of day — morning coffee.).

examples.en: This is my favorite moment on the trip — eating together.
examples.ko: 여행 중에 이때가 제일 좋아. 다 같이 밥 먹는 시간.

examples.en: This is my favorite time of day — morning coffee.
examples.ko: 하루 중에 이때가 제일 좋아. 커피 마시는 아침.

examples.en: This is the moment I love most. Everyone is smiling.
examples.ko: 이때가 제일 좋아. 모두가 웃는 순간이야.

literal_en: How about that restaurant? I heard the reviews are ~
usage_en: Casually suggest or ask about an option or idea. Say what you need, then add 은 어때 at the end. Common uses: 저 식당은 어때? 후기가 좋던데. (How about that restaurant? I heard the reviews are great.) or 내일은 어때? 시간 있어? (How about tomorrow? Are you free?).

examples.en: How about that restaurant? I heard the reviews are great.
How about tomorrow? Are you free?
How about pizza? Let's order it together.

usage_en: Share that you felt hurt or let down because of someone's actions. Say what you need, then add 서운했어요 at the end. Common uses: 연락이 없어서 서운했어요. (I felt hurt because there was no contact.) or 그 말이 서운했어요. (Those words hurt me.).

examples.en: I felt hurt because there was no contact.
Those words hurt me.
I felt let down, but I understand.

usage_en: Acknowledge politely that you understand someone's feelings or intentions. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 마음은 알아요. 하지만 이건 힘들어요. (I understand your feelings, but this is difficult.) or 마음은 알아요. 걱정해줘서 고마워요. (I understand how you feel. Thank you for caring.).

examples.en: I understand your feelings, but this is difficult.
I understand how you feel. Thank you for caring.
I understand your feelings. I felt the same way.

usage_en: Express relief after finally saying something that was on your mind. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 말하고 나니까 후련해요. 오래 참았어요. (I feel relieved now that I said it. I held it in for a long time.) or 속상했는데 말하고 나니까 후련해요. (I was upset, but saying it out loud made me feel better.).

examples.en: I feel relieved now that I said it. I held it in for a long time.
I was upset, but saying it out loud made me feel better.
I feel so relieved after talking it out. Thank you for listening.

usage_en: Ask someone what their dream or aspiration in life is. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 꿈이 뭐예요? 나중에 뭐 하고 싶어요? (What's your dream? What do you want to do in the future?) or 어릴 때 꿈이 뭐예요? 지금도 같아요? (What was your dream when you were young? Is it still the same?).

examples.en: What's your dream? What do you want to do in the future?
examples.ko: 꿈이 뭐예요? 나중에 뭐 하고 싶어요?

examples.en: What was your dream when you were young? Is it still the same?
examples.ko: 어릴 때 꿈이 뭐예요? 지금도 같아요?

examples.en: What's your dream? It sounds amazing.

literal_en: I want to become a Korean ~
usage_en: Say what profession or role you want to become in the future. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 한국어 선생님이 되고 싶어요. (I want to become a Korean teacher.) or 유명한 요리사가 되고 싶어요. (I want to become a famous chef.).

examples.en: I want to become a Korean teacher.
I want to become a famous chef.
I want to become a writer.

usage_en: Confess that you feel like giving up on something difficult. Say what you need, then add 포기하고 싶어요 at the end. Common uses: 너무 힘들어서 포기하고 싶어요. (It's so hard that I want to give up.) or 가끔 포기하고 싶어요. 하지만 계속해요. (Sometimes I want to give up. But I keep going.).

examples.en: It's so hard that I want to give up.
Sometimes I want to give up. But I keep going.
I wanted to give up, but my friend cheered me on.

literal_en: Where do I throw away this ~?
usage_en: Ask casually where to throw something away or how to recycle it. Say what you need, then add 어디에 버려 at the end. Common uses: 이 종이 어디에 버려? (Where do I throw away this paper?) or 음식물 쓰레기 어디에 버려? (Where do I throw away food waste?).

examples.en: Where do I throw away this paper?
Where do I throw away food waste?
Where do I throw away plastic? Do I have to separate it?
examples.ko: 플라스틱 어디에 버려? 따로 분리해야 해?

literal_en: Do you do recycling thoroughly? I think it's ~
usage_en: Ask casually if someone does something in a thorough, careful way. Just place a noun before 철저히 해 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 분리수거 철저히 해? 중요한 것 같아. (Do you do recycling thoroughly? I think it's important.) or 운동 후에 스트레칭 철저히 해? (Do you do thorough stretching after working out?).

examples.en: Do you do recycling thoroughly? I think it's important.
examples.ko: 분리수거 철저히 해? 중요한 것 같아.

examples.en: Do you do thorough stretching after working out?
Do you clean thoroughly? It looks spotless.

literal_en: I should pay more attention to my ~
usage_en: Decides to pay closer attention to something from now on. Say what you need, then add 신경 써야겠어 at the end. Common uses: 건강 더 신경 써야겠어. (I should pay more attention to my health.) or 발음 신경 써야겠어. (I need to be more careful about my pronunciation.).

examples.en: I should pay more attention to my health.
I need to be more careful about my pronunciation.
I should pay more attention to the environment.

usage_en: Say that feelings or ideas are hard to put into words. Say what you need, then add 말로 표현하기 어려워요 at the end. Common uses: 이 감정은 말로 표현하기 어려워요. (This feeling is hard to put into words.) or 말로 표현하기 어려워요, 그냥 좋아요. (It's hard to explain — I just like it.).

examples.en: This feeling is hard to put into words.
It's hard to explain — I just like it.
The taste is difficult to describe in words.

usage_en: Ask if someone relates to or understands a specific feeling you have. Say what you need, then add 이 느낌 알아요 at the end. Common uses: 시험 전날 긴장되는 느낌, 이 느낌 알아요? (The nervous feeling before a test — do you know it?) or 오랜만에 고향 음식 먹는 느낌, 이 느낌 알아요? (Eating hometown food after a long time — do you know that feeling?).

examples.en: The nervous feeling before a test — do you know it?
examples.ko: 시험 전날 긴장되는 느낌, 이 느낌 알아요?

examples.en: Eating hometown food after a long time — do you know that feeling?
examples.ko: 오랜만에 고향 음식 먹는 느낌, 이 느낌 알아요?

examples.en: The Friday afternoon feeling — do you know it?
examples.ko: 금요일 오후 느낌, 이 느낌 알아요?

usage_en: Describe a feeling you have for no clear or explainable reason. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 왠지 모르게 오늘 기분이 좋아요. (For some reason, I'm in a good mood today.) or 왠지 모르게 슬퍼요. (For no particular reason, I feel sad.).

examples.en: For some reason, I'm in a good mood today.
For no particular reason, I feel sad.
For some reason, I really like this song.

usage_en: Say something perfectly matches an exact feeling or expectation. Say what you need, then add 딱 이 느낌이에요 at the end. Common uses: 제가 찾던 게 딱 이 느낌이에요. (This is exactly the feeling I was looking for.) or 딱 이 느낌이에요! 너무 좋아요. (This is exactly it! I love it.).

examples.en: This is exactly the feeling I was looking for.
examples.ko: 제가 찾던 게 딱 이 느낌이에요.

examples.en: This is exactly it! I love it.
Autumn is exactly this feeling.

usage_en: Acknowledge casually that a misunderstanding occurred between people. Say what you need, then add 오해가 있었어 at the end. Common uses: 우리 사이에 오해가 있었어. (There was a misunderstanding between us.) or 오해가 있었어. 내 말을 잘못 들은 것 같아. (There was a misunderstanding. I think you misheard me.).

examples.en: There was a misunderstanding between us.
There was a misunderstanding. I think you misheard me.
examples.ko: 오해가 있었어. 내 말을 잘못 들은 것 같아.

examples.en: There was a misunderstanding. I hope we can clear it up now.

usage_en: Clarify that something you said wasn't meant a certain way. Just place a noun before 뜻이 아니었어 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 화내려는 뜻이 아니었어. (I didn't mean to get angry.) or 그런 뜻이 아니었어. 오해하지 마. (I didn't mean it that way. Don't misunderstand.).

examples.en: I didn't mean to get angry.
I didn't mean it that way. Don't misunderstand.
I didn't mean it sarcastically.

usage_en: Assure someone you fully understand their feelings or situation. Say what you need, then add 충분히 이해해 at the end. Common uses: 네 상황 충분히 이해해. (I fully understand your situation.) or 화난 이유 충분히 이해해. (I completely understand why you're angry.).

examples.en: I fully understand your situation.
I completely understand why you're angry.
I totally understand. Don't worry.

usage_en: Announce that you or someone passed an exam or was accepted somewhere. Just place a noun before 합격했어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 시험에 합격했어요! (I passed the exam!) or 면접에 합격했어요. (I passed the interview.).

examples.en: I passed the exam!
I passed the interview.
I passed the TOPIK!

usage_en: Celebrate finally accomplishing something after a long effort. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 드디어 해냈어요! 1년 만에 완성했어요. (I finally did it! I completed it after a year.) or 포기 안 하고 드디어 해냈어요. (I didn't give up and finally made it.).

examples.en: I finally did it! I completed it after a year.
I didn't give up and finally made it.
I finally did it. I feel like crying.
examples.ko: 드디어 해냈어요. 눈물 날 것 같아요.

usage_en: Praise someone for getting through a difficult situation well. Say what you need, then add 잘 이겨냈어요 at the end. Common uses: 힘든 시간을 잘 이겨냈어요. (You got through the tough time well.) or 정말 잘 이겨냈어요. 대단해요. (You really got through it well. You're amazing.).

examples.en: You got through the tough time well.
You really got through it well. You're amazing.
You got through it well on your own.

usage_en: Recommend trying a particular food to a friend. Say what you need, then add 먹어봐 at the end. Common uses: 이거 한번 먹어봐. 진짜 맛있어. (Try this. It's really delicious.) or 떡볶이 먹어봐. 좋아할 거야. (Try tteokbokki. You'll like it.).

examples.en: Try this. It's really delicious.
Try tteokbokki. You'll like it.
Try this ramen. It's surprisingly good.

usage_en: Say something is far more or less than you expected. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 생각보다 훨씬 맛있어. (It's way more delicious than I thought.) or 생각보다 훨씬 어려워. (It's way harder than I expected.).

examples.en: It's way more delicious than I thought.
It's way harder than I expected.
It's way more fun than I thought.

usage_en: Tell a friend something is so addictive you can't stop enjoying it. Say what you need, then add 중독성 있어 at the end. Common uses: 이 노래 중독성 있어. 계속 듣게 돼. (This song is addictive. I keep listening to it.) or 이 게임 중독성 있어. (This game is addictive.).

examples.en: This song is addictive. I keep listening to it.
examples.ko: 이 노래 중독성 있어. 계속 듣게 돼.

examples.en: This game is addictive.
This food is addictive — I keep eating it.
examples.ko: 이 음식 중독성 있어서 자꾸 먹게 돼.

usage_en: Simply express that you feel genuinely happy in the present moment. Say what you need, then add 행복해요 at the end. Common uses: 지금 이 순간 행복해요. (I'm happy in this moment.) or 여기 오니까 행복해요. (I'm happy being here.).

examples.en: I'm happy in this moment.
I'm happy being here.
I'm happy when I'm with friends.

usage_en: Express that you enjoy a particular activity or type of thing. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 음악 듣는 게 좋아요. (I like listening to music.) or 혼자 걷는 게 좋아요. (I like walking alone.).

examples.en: I like listening to music.
I like walking alone.
I like cooking.

usage_en: Say that ordinary everyday moments feel precious and meaningful. Say what you need, then add 이런 일상이 소중해요 at the end. Common uses: 같이 밥 먹는 이런 일상이 소중해요. (These everyday moments of eating together are precious.) or 평범해 보여도 이런 일상이 소중해요. (It may seem ordinary, but these daily moments are precious.).

examples.en: These everyday moments of eating together are precious.
examples.ko: 같이 밥 먹는 이런 일상이 소중해요.

examples.en: It may seem ordinary, but these daily moments are precious.
These everyday moments are precious. I hope they last a long time.
examples.ko: 이런 일상이 소중해요. 오래오래 지속되면 좋겠어요.

usage_en: Reassure a friend that something is simple once you know how. Say what you need, then add 알고 보면 쉬워 at the end. Common uses: 한국어 문법, 알고 보면 쉬워. (Korean grammar is easy once you understand it.) or 어려워 보여도 알고 보면 쉬워. (It looks hard, but once you know it, it's easy.).

examples.en: Korean grammar is easy once you understand it.
It looks hard, but once you know it, it's easy.
This machine is easy once you know how.

usage_en: Point out the most important trick or key element to a friend. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 반죽을 충분히 치대는 게 포인트야. (Kneading the dough well is the key point.) or 이 문장에서 이게 포인트야. (This is the key part in this sentence.).

examples.en: Kneading the dough well is the key point.
This is the key part in this sentence.
This is the key point. Remember it well.

usage_en: Express happiness about getting together as a group. Just place a noun before 다 같이 모이니까 좋아요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 오랜만에 다 같이 모이니까 좋아요. (It's great that we're all gathered after a long time.) or 다 같이 모이니까 좋아요. 자주 봐요. (It's nice that we're all here. Let's meet more often.).

examples.en: It's great that we're all gathered after a long time.
It's nice that we're all here. Let's meet more often.
examples.ko: 다 같이 모이니까 좋아요. 자주 봐요.

examples.en: I love that we're all together like this.

usage_en: Recall or refer to the time when you first met someone. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 처음 만났을 때 많이 떨렸어요. (I was very nervous when we first met.) or 처음 만났을 때가 기억나요? (Do you remember when we first met?).

examples.en: I was very nervous when we first met.
Do you remember when we first met?
We've been close since we first met.

usage_en: Credit everyone around you for your success or happiness. Say what you need, then add 여러분 덕분이에요 at the end. Common uses: 여기까지 올 수 있었던 건 여러분 덕분이에요. (I was able to come this far thanks to all of you.) or 여러분 덕분이에요. 진심으로 감사해요. (It's all thanks to you. I'm truly grateful.).

examples.en: I was able to come this far thanks to all of you.
examples.ko: 여기까지 올 수 있었던 건 여러분 덕분이에요.

examples.en: It's all thanks to you. I'm truly grateful.
This award is because of all of you.

usage_en: Ask politely for continued goodwill and support going forward. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 앞으로도 잘 부탁해요. 잘 지내봐요. (Please continue to take care of me. Let's get along well.) or 처음이지만 앞으로도 잘 부탁해요. (It's my first time, but please take good care of me going forward.).

examples.en: Please continue to take care of me. Let's get along well.
It's my first time, but please take good care of me going forward.
I look forward to working with you. I'm glad we're together.

usage_en: Ask how long someone plans to stay at a place. Just place a noun before 얼마나 있을 거예요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 한국에 얼마나 있을 거예요? (How long will you be in Korea?) or 여기에 얼마나 있을 거예요? (How long are you going to stay here?).

examples.en: How long will you be in Korea?
How long are you going to stay here?
How long will you be in Seoul? Let's hang out.
examples.ko: 서울에 얼마나 있을 거예요? 같이 놀아요.

usage_en: Declare you will do something in pursuit of your dream. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 꿈을 위해 열심히 공부할 거예요. (I'll study hard for my dream.) or 힘들어도 꿈을 위해 할 거예요. (Even if it's hard, I'll do it for my dream.).

examples.en: I'll study hard for my dream.
Even if it's hard, I'll do it for my dream.
I'll even move for my dream.

usage_en: Warn that you have to wait in line at a popular place. Just place a noun before 줄 서야 해요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 맛집이라 줄 서야 해요. (It's a popular restaurant, so you have to wait in line.) or 아침 일찍부터 줄 서야 해요. (You have to line up early in the morning.).

examples.en: It's a popular restaurant, so you have to wait in line.
You have to line up early in the morning.
You always have to wait in line there.

usage_en: Ask if there is currently a wait or waitlist at a restaurant. Just place a noun before 웨이팅 있어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 지금 웨이팅 있어요? (Is there a wait right now?) or 웨이팅 있어요? 얼마나 기다려야 해요? (Is there a wait? How long do I need to wait?).

examples.en: Is there a wait right now?
Is there a wait? How long do I need to wait?
There's a wait. I need to wait about 30 minutes.

usage_en: Strongly recommend a place as an absolute must-visit destination. Just place a noun before 꼭 와봐야 할 곳이에요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 경복궁은 꼭 와봐야 할 곳이에요. (Gyeongbokgung Palace is a place you must visit.) or 한국에 오면 꼭 와봐야 할 곳이에요. (If you come to Korea, this is a must-visit place.).

examples.en: Gyeongbokgung Palace is a place you must visit.
If you come to Korea, this is a must-visit place.
examples.ko: 한국에 오면 꼭 와봐야 할 곳이에요.

examples.en: This village is a place you absolutely must visit.
examples.ko: 이 마을은 꼭 와봐야 할 곳이에요.

usage_en: Express shock or disbelief at something surprising or incredible. Just place a noun before 믿기지 않아 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 합격했어. 믿기지 않아. (I passed. I can't believe it.) or 10년이 지났어. 믿기지 않아. (Ten years have passed. I can't believe it.).

examples.en: I passed. I can't believe it.
Ten years have passed. I can't believe it.
Is this real? I can't believe it.

usage_en: Compare the present situation to how things were at the very start. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 처음에 비하면 한국어가 많이 늘었어요. (Compared to the beginning, my Korean has improved a lot.) or 처음에 비하면 많이 달라졌어요. (Compared to the start, a lot has changed.).

examples.en: Compared to the beginning, my Korean has improved a lot.
Compared to the start, a lot has changed.
Compared to the beginning, I've gained much more confidence.

usage_en: Reflect that it was the right choice not to give up. Just place a noun before 포기 안 하길 잘했어 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 힘들었지만 포기 안 하길 잘했어. (It was hard, but I'm glad I didn't give up.) or 포기 안 하길 잘했어. 결국 해냈어. (I'm glad I didn't give up. I finally did it.).

examples.en: It was hard, but I'm glad I didn't give up.
I'm glad I didn't give up. I finally did it.
examples.ko: 포기 안 하길 잘했어. 결국 해냈어.

examples.en: Good thing I didn't give up — all for this moment.
examples.ko: 포기 안 하길 잘했어. 이 순간을 위해서.

usage_en: Share something you heard said about a topic or place. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 거기 맛있다고 하던데. (I heard it's delicious there.) or 내일 비 온다고 하던데. (I heard it's going to rain tomorrow.).

examples.en: I heard it's delicious there.
I heard it's going to rain tomorrow.
I heard that café has a great atmosphere.

literal_en: I heard the line there is really ~
usage_en: Pass along second-hand information you heard from someone else. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 거기 줄이 엄청 길다더라. (I heard the line there is really long.) or 그 영화 재밌다더라. (I heard that movie is interesting.).

examples.en: I heard the line there is really long.
I heard that movie is interesting.
I heard this exam is going to be tough.

literal_en: I didn't know it would be this ~
usage_en: Express surprise at learning something you genuinely didn't know. Say what you need, then add 는 줄 몰랐어 at the end. Common uses: 이렇게 맛있는 줄 몰랐어. (I didn't know it would be this delicious.) or 한국어 배우는 게 이렇게 재밌는 줄 몰랐어. (I didn't know learning Korean would be this fun.).

examples.en: I didn't know it would be this delicious.
I didn't know learning Korean would be this fun.
examples.ko: 한국어 배우는 게 이렇게 재밌는 줄 몰랐어.

examples.en: I didn't know you thought that way.

usage_en: Describe naturally how something came to happen or change. Say what you need, then add 게 됐어요 at the end. Common uses: 한국에 살게 됐어요. (I ended up living in Korea.) or 그 사람이랑 친하게 됐어요. (I ended up becoming close with that person.).

examples.en: I ended up living in Korea.
I ended up becoming close with that person.
I ended up doing this job.

literal_en: As I kept practicing every day, my skills ~
usage_en: Describe a gradual result that came from repeatedly doing something. Say what you need, then add 다 보니까 at the end. Common uses: 매일 연습하다 보니까 실력이 늘었어요. (As I kept practicing every day, my skills improved.) or 한국 드라마 보다 보니까 한국어가 늘었어요. (As I kept watching Korean dramas, my Korean got better.).

examples.en: As I kept practicing every day, my skills improved.
As I kept watching Korean dramas, my Korean got better.
examples.ko: 한국 드라마 보다 보니까 한국어가 늘었어요.

examples.en: As I kept doing it, I got used to it.

literal_en: If you keep practicing, you'll get ~
usage_en: Encourage that natural improvement comes with continued effort. Say what you need, then add 하다 보면 at the end. Common uses: 계속 연습하다 보면 늘어요. (If you keep practicing, you'll get better.) or 자꾸 먹다 보면 익숙해져요. (If you keep eating it, you'll get used to it.).

examples.en: If you keep practicing, you'll get better.
If you keep eating it, you'll get used to it.
If you do it every day, it'll get easier.

literal_en: For a first attempt, you did really ~
usage_en: Say someone does surprisingly well given their circumstances. Just place a noun before 한 것치고는 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 처음 한 것치고는 잘했어요. (For a first attempt, you did really well.) or 배운 지 한 달 된 것치고는 실력이 좋아요. (For someone who's studied for a month, your skills are great.).

examples.en: For a first attempt, you did really well.
For someone who's studied for a month, your skills are great.
examples.ko: 배운 지 한 달 된 것치고는 실력이 좋아요.

examples.en: For something you made alone, it's really tasty.

usage_en: Say that even so, certain limits or principles still apply. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 아무리 그래도 그건 너무해. (Even so, that's too much.) or 아무리 바빠도 밥은 먹어야지. (Even if you're busy, you still have to eat.).

examples.en: Even so, that's too much.
Even if you're busy, you still have to eat.
Even so, lying is not okay.

usage_en: Politely say you're not really sure about something. Say what you need, then add 잘 모르겠는데요 at the end. Common uses: 그 문제는 잘 모르겠는데요. (I'm not really sure about that question.) or 거기 어떻게 가는지 잘 모르겠는데요. (I'm not sure how to get there.).

examples.en: I'm not really sure about that question.
I'm not sure how to get there.
I'm not sure. Let me look into it.

usage_en: Say you need more time to think something through before deciding. Say what you need, then add 좀 더 생각해 봐야겠어요 at the end. Common uses: 지금 당장 결정 못 하겠어요. 좀 더 생각해 봐야겠어요. (I can't decide right now. I need to think more.) or 좀 더 생각해 봐야겠어요. 내일 알려드릴게요. (I need to think it over. I'll let you know tomorrow.).

examples.en: I can't decide right now. I need to think more.
examples.ko: 지금 당장 결정 못 하겠어요. 좀 더 생각해 봐야겠어요.

examples.en: I need to think it over. I'll let you know tomorrow.
examples.ko: 좀 더 생각해 봐야겠어요. 내일 알려드릴게요.

examples.en: This is an important decision, so I need to think more.
examples.ko: 이건 중요한 결정이라 좀 더 생각해 봐야겠어요.

usage_en: Suggest doing something as a first step for now. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 일단은 먹어요. 이야기는 나중에. (Let's eat first. We'll talk later.) or 일단은 앉아요. (For now, have a seat.).

examples.en: Let's eat first. We'll talk later.
For now, have a seat.
For now, let's try. Think about it after.

usage_en: Ask if someone noticed or picked up on something subtle. Say what you need, then add 눈치챘어요 at the end. Common uses: 제가 긴장한 거 눈치챘어요? (Did you notice that I was nervous?) or 제가 힌트 줬는데 눈치챘어요? (I gave you a hint — did you catch on?).

examples.en: Did you notice that I was nervous?
I gave you a hint — did you catch on?
Did you notice something changed?

usage_en: Say you're starting to get the feel or hang of something. Say what you need, then add 감이 잡혀요 at the end. Common uses: 설명 들으니까 감이 잡혀요. (After hearing the explanation, I'm getting the hang of it.) or 이제 조금 감이 잡혀요. (I'm starting to get the feel for it now.).

examples.en: After hearing the explanation, I'm getting the hang of it.
I'm starting to get the feel for it now.
I'm getting a feel for Korean pronunciation.

usage_en: Say something is obvious just from looking at it. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 딱 봐도 비싸 보여요. (You can tell just by looking that it's expensive.) or 딱 봐도 맛있겠어요. (Just looking at it, you can tell it'll be delicious.).

examples.en: You can tell just by looking that it's expensive.
Just looking at it, you can tell it'll be delicious.
I can tell just by looking. That's the answer.

usage_en: Say something happens all the time and is no big deal. Say what you need, then add 흔한 일이야 at the end. Common uses: 지하철 놓치는 건 흔한 일이야. (Missing the subway is a common thing.) or 실수하는 건 흔한 일이야. 너무 신경 쓰지 마. (Making mistakes is common. Don't worry too much about it.).

examples.en: Missing the subway is a common thing.
Making mistakes is common. Don't worry too much about it.
examples.ko: 실수하는 건 흔한 일이야. 너무 신경 쓰지 마.

examples.en: That kind of thing happens all the time.

usage_en: Reveal an unexpected quality someone or something has once you know them. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 그 사람, 알고 보면 정말 친절해. (Once you get to know them, they're really kind.) or 알고 보면 한국어 발음 규칙이 간단해. (Once you know it, Korean pronunciation rules are simple.).

examples.en: Once you get to know them, they're really kind.
examples.ko: 그 사람, 알고 보면 정말 친절해.

examples.en: Once you know it, Korean pronunciation rules are simple.
examples.ko: 알고 보면 한국어 발음 규칙이 간단해.

examples.en: It looks hard, but once you know it, it's fun.

usage_en: Express feeling pressured or overwhelmed by expectations or a situation. Say what you need, then add 부담스러워요 at the end. Common uses: 선물이 너무 커서 부담스러워요. (The gift is so big that I feel pressured.) or 기대가 너무 크면 부담스러워요. (When expectations are too high, I feel overwhelmed.).

examples.en: The gift is so big that I feel pressured.
When expectations are too high, I feel overwhelmed.
Being told to present suddenly makes me feel pressured.

usage_en: Politely ask permission before giving an honest or direct opinion. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 솔직하게 말해도 돼요? 조금 아쉬워요. (Can I be honest? I'm a little disappointed.) or 솔직하게 말해도 돼요? 이게 더 잘 어울려요. (Can I speak freely? This one suits you better.).

examples.en: Can I be honest? I'm a little disappointed.
Can I speak freely? This one suits you better.
examples.ko: 솔직하게 말해도 돼요? 이게 더 잘 어울려요.

examples.en: Can I be honest? I think you should reconsider.
examples.ko: 솔직하게 말해도 돼요? 다시 생각해보는 게 좋을 것 같아요.

usage_en: Say you have become much more comfortable in a situation. Say what you need, then add 이제 많이 편해졌어요 at the end. Common uses: 한국 생활이 이제 많이 편해졌어요. (Life in Korea has become much more comfortable now.) or 처음엔 어색했는데 이제 많이 편해졌어요. (It was awkward at first, but now I'm a lot more comfortable.).

examples.en: Life in Korea has become much more comfortable now.
It was awkward at first, but now I'm a lot more comfortable.
I'm a lot more at ease now. Thank you.

usage_en: Ask honestly whether you come across as a foreigner. Say what you need, then add 외국인 티 나요 at the end. Common uses: 제가 말할 때 외국인 티 나요? (Do I seem like a foreigner when I speak?) or 외국인 티 나요? 발음 때문에요? (Do I seem like a foreigner? Is it because of my pronunciation?).

examples.en: Do I seem like a foreigner when I speak?
examples.ko: 제가 말할 때 외국인 티 나요?

examples.en: Do I seem like a foreigner? Is it because of my pronunciation?
Do I not seem like a foreigner anymore?

usage_en: Say that Korean now feels comfortable and natural to use. Say what you need, then add 이제 한국말이 편해요 at the end. Common uses: 처음엔 힘들었는데 이제 한국말이 편해요. (It was hard at first, but now Korean feels comfortable.) or 이제 한국말이 편해요. 생각도 한국어로 해요. (Korean is comfortable for me now. I even think in Korean.).

examples.en: It was hard at first, but now Korean feels comfortable.
Korean is comfortable for me now. I even think in Korean.
examples.ko: 이제 한국말이 편해요. 생각도 한국어로 해요.

examples.en: Korean is natural for me now. Sometimes it's even easier than English.
examples.ko: 이제 한국말이 편해요. 영어보다 더 편할 때도 있어요.

usage_en: Show deep fluency by mentioning you even dream in Korean now. Just place a noun before 한국어로 꿈도 꿔요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 요즘 한국어로 꿈도 꿔요. (Lately, I even dream in Korean.) or 한국어로 꿈도 꿔요. 실력이 는 것 같아요. (I even dream in Korean. I think my skills are improving.).

examples.en: Lately, I even dream in Korean.
I even dream in Korean. I think my skills are improving.
examples.ko: 한국어로 꿈도 꿔요. 실력이 는 것 같아요.

examples.en: Do you really dream in Korean? That's amazing!

usage_en: Say you prefer local hidden spots over typical tourist attractions. Just place a noun before 관광지보다 로컬이 좋아 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 저는 관광지보다 로컬이 좋아요. (I prefer local spots over tourist attractions.) or 관광지보다 로컬이 좋아. 더 진짜 같아. (I like local places better than tourist spots. They feel more authentic.).

examples.en: I prefer local spots over tourist attractions.
I like local places better than tourist spots. They feel more authentic.
examples.ko: 관광지보다 로컬이 좋아. 더 진짜 같아.

examples.en: I prefer local cafes over tourist places.

usage_en: Describe a place as somewhere locals actually go, not a tourist trap. Just place a noun before 현지인들이 가는 곳이야 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 여기 현지인들이 가는 곳이야. 관광객은 별로 없어. (This is a place locals go. Not many tourists here.) or 현지인들이 가는 곳이야. 더 저렴하고 맛있어. (It's where the locals go. Cheaper and more delicious.).

examples.en: This is a place locals go. Not many tourists here.
examples.ko: 여기 현지인들이 가는 곳이야. 관광객은 별로 없어.

examples.en: It's where the locals go. Cheaper and more delicious.
examples.ko: 현지인들이 가는 곳이야. 더 저렴하고 맛있어.

examples.en: This market is a place the locals frequent.

usage_en: Call out a lesser-known but wonderful hidden gem of a place. Just place a noun before 숨겨진 명소야 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 여기 숨겨진 명소야. 사람이 별로 없어. (This place is a hidden gem. Not many people know about it.) or 이 골목이 숨겨진 명소야. (This alley is a hidden gem.).

examples.en: This place is a hidden gem. Not many people know about it.
examples.ko: 여기 숨겨진 명소야. 사람이 별로 없어.

examples.en: This alley is a hidden gem.
It's a hidden gem that tourists don't know about.

usage_en: Tell someone something is very popular and trending right now. Say what you need, then add 요즘 핫해요 at the end. Common uses: 이 카페 요즘 핫해요. (This cafe is really popular these days.) or 이 드라마 요즘 핫해요. 봤어요? (This drama is trending right now. Have you seen it?).

examples.en: This cafe is really popular these days.
This drama is trending right now. Have you seen it?
This place is hot right now. It keeps popping up on social media.
examples.ko: 이 곳 요즘 핫해요. SNS에 자꾸 나와요.

usage_en: Say something is totally dominating as the current mainstream trend. Say what you need, then add 완전 대세예요 at the end. Common uses: 이 스타일 완전 대세예요. (This style is totally the trend right now.) or 요즘 이 음식이 완전 대세예요. (This food is completely trending right now.).

examples.en: This style is totally the trend right now.
This food is completely trending right now.
That idol group is totally dominating the scene.

usage_en: Say something or someone is currently rising in popularity. Say what you need, then add 떠오르는 중이에요 at the end. Common uses: 이 가수 요즘 떠오르는 중이에요. (This singer is on the rise these days.) or 이 동네가 요즘 떠오르는 중이에요. (This neighborhood is gaining popularity recently.).

examples.en: This singer is on the rise these days.
This neighborhood is gaining popularity recently.
This app is on the rise. Have you tried it?

usage_en: Reluctantly admit something is true without fully agreeing with it. Say what you need, then add 아니라고 할 순 없지 at the end. Common uses: 비싸긴 한데, 아니라고 할 순 없지. (It is expensive, but I can't say it's not worth it.) or 좀 어렵긴 한데 아니라고 할 순 없지. (It's a bit hard, but I can't deny it.).

examples.en: It is expensive, but I can't say it's not worth it.
examples.ko: 비싸긴 한데, 아니라고 할 순 없지.

examples.en: It's a bit hard, but I can't deny it.
examples.ko: 좀 어렵긴 한데 아니라고 할 순 없지.

examples.en: It tastes good, but I can't deny it's not healthy.
examples.ko: 맛있긴 한데 건강에 안 좋다는 건 아니라고 할 순 없지.

usage_en: Gently push back on a generalization or assumption. Say what you need, then add 꼭 그런 건 아니야 at the end. Common uses: 비싼 게 다 좋은 건 꼭 그런 건 아니야. (Expensive doesn't always mean good. That's not necessarily true.) or 한국 음식이 다 매운 건 꼭 그런 건 아니야. (Not all Korean food is spicy. That's not necessarily true.).

examples.en: Expensive doesn't always mean good. That's not necessarily true.
examples.ko: 비싼 게 다 좋은 건 꼭 그런 건 아니야.

examples.en: Not all Korean food is spicy. That's not necessarily true.
examples.ko: 한국 음식이 다 매운 건 꼭 그런 건 아니야.

examples.en: That's not necessarily so. It varies by person.
examples.ko: 꼭 그런 건 아니야. 사람마다 달라.

usage_en: Say an explanation or argument makes sense to you. Say what you need, then add 말이 되네요 at the end. Common uses: 그렇게 생각하면 말이 되네요. (Thinking about it that way, it makes sense.) or 설명 들으니까 말이 되네요. (After hearing the explanation, it makes sense.).

examples.en: Thinking about it that way, it makes sense.
After hearing the explanation, it makes sense.
That makes sense. Now I understand.

usage_en: Point out that something is inconsistent or doesn't add up. Just place a noun before 앞뒤가 안 맞아요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 이야기가 앞뒤가 안 맞아요. (The story doesn't add up.) or 말이 앞뒤가 안 맞아요. 다시 설명해 주세요. (What you're saying is inconsistent. Please explain again.).

examples.en: The story doesn't add up.
What you're saying is inconsistent. Please explain again.
examples.ko: 말이 앞뒤가 안 맞아요. 다시 설명해 주세요.

examples.en: It doesn't add up. Something seems off.

usage_en: State what happened or what will happen in the end. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 결국엔 잘 됐어요. (In the end, it worked out well.) or 결국엔 포기했어요. (In the end, I gave up.).

examples.en: In the end, it worked out well.
In the end, I gave up.
In the end, I was right.

usage_en: Share that something hurt your feelings or made you feel upset. Say what you need, then add 속상했어요 at the end. Common uses: 그 말 듣고 많이 속상했어요. (I was really upset when I heard that.) or 약속을 안 지켜서 속상했어요. (I was upset because you didn't keep your promise.).

examples.en: I was really upset when I heard that.
I was upset because you didn't keep your promise.
I was upset, but I'm okay now.

usage_en: Express feeling wrongly blamed or treated unfairly. Say what you need, then add 억울했어요 at the end. Common uses: 내 잘못이 아닌데 혼나서 억울했어요. (I felt wronged because I was scolded for something that wasn't my fault.) or 오해 받아서 억울했어요. (I felt wrongly accused because of a misunderstanding.).

examples.en: I felt wronged because I was scolded for something that wasn't my fault.
I felt wrongly accused because of a misunderstanding.
I felt unfairly treated. It wasn't me.

usage_en: Encourage someone to consider the other person's perspective. Say what you need, then add 상대방 입장에서 생각해봐 at the end. Common uses: 화내기 전에 상대방 입장에서 생각해봐. (Before getting angry, think from the other person's perspective.) or 상대방 입장에서 생각해봐. 그 사람도 힘들었을 거야. (Think from the other person's perspective. They must have had a hard time too.).

examples.en: Before getting angry, think from the other person's perspective.
Think from the other person's perspective. They must have had a hard time too.
examples.ko: 상대방 입장에서 생각해봐. 그 사람도 힘들었을 거야.

examples.en: Try thinking from the other person's side. It'll look very different.
examples.ko: 상대방 입장에서 생각해봐. 많이 달라 보일 거야.

usage_en: Tell a friend you understand their feelings even if you can't change things. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Common uses: 마음은 알아. 그래도 조금만 기다려봐. (I understand how you feel. But just wait a little.) or 마음은 알아. 많이 힘들지? (I know how you feel. It must be really tough, right?).

examples.en: I understand how you feel. But just wait a little.
I know how you feel. It must be really tough, right?
I know how you feel. I've been there too.

usage_en: Promise a friend you will stay by their side for support. Just place a noun before 내가 옆에 있을게 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 힘들어도 내가 옆에 있을게. (Even when it's tough, I'll be by your side.) or 걱정 마. 내가 옆에 있을게. (Don't worry. I'll be right here with you.).

examples.en: Even when it's tough, I'll be by your side.
Don't worry. I'll be right here with you.
I'll always be by your side.

usage_en: Tease that a story or situation has a surprising twist ending. Say what you need, then add 반전 있어요 at the end. Common uses: 이 영화 반전 있어요. 끝까지 봐요. (This movie has a twist. Watch until the end.) or 이 이야기 반전 있어요! (This story has a plot twist!).

examples.en: This movie has a twist. Watch until the end.
examples.ko: 이 영화 반전 있어요. 끝까지 봐요.

examples.en: This story has a plot twist!
There's a twist at the end. I was really surprised.

usage_en: Say something leaves a lingering impression long after it ends. Say what you need, then add 여운이 남아요 at the end. Common uses: 이 영화, 보고 나서도 여운이 남아요. (Even after watching this movie, the feeling lingers.) or 그 말이 아직도 여운이 남아요. (Those words still leave a lingering impression.).

examples.en: Even after watching this movie, the feeling lingers.
examples.ko: 이 영화, 보고 나서도 여운이 남아요.

examples.en: Those words still leave a lingering impression.
Even though the music ended, the feeling stays.

usage_en: Say you get totally absorbed and lost in something you're doing. Say what you need, then add 몰입이 돼요 at the end. Common uses: 이 책 읽으면 몰입이 돼요. (When I read this book, I get completely absorbed.) or 이 드라마 몰입이 돼서 밤새 봤어요. (I got so absorbed in this drama that I watched it all night.).

examples.en: When I read this book, I get completely absorbed.
I got so absorbed in this drama that I watched it all night.
examples.ko: 이 드라마 몰입이 돼서 밤새 봤어요.

examples.en: When I play this game, I get absorbed and lose track of time.
examples.ko: 이 게임 하면 몰입이 돼서 시간 가는 줄 몰라요.

usage_en: Describe being inexplicably drawn to something without a clear reason. Say what you need, then add 어딘가 모르게 끌려요 at the end. Common uses: 이 그림, 어딘가 모르게 끌려요. (I'm drawn to this painting for some reason.) or 처음 봤는데 어딘가 모르게 끌려요. (I just saw it, but I'm inexplicably drawn to it.).

examples.en: I'm drawn to this painting for some reason.
I just saw it, but I'm inexplicably drawn to it.
For some reason, I'm drawn to Korean.

usage_en: Express not wanting to leave a place or moment you love. Say what you need, then add 떠나기 싫어 at the end. Common uses: 한국이 너무 좋아서 떠나기 싫어. (I love Korea so much that I don't want to leave.) or 여기 너무 편해서 떠나기 싫어. (It's so comfortable here that I don't want to go.).

examples.en: I love Korea so much that I don't want to leave.
It's so comfortable here that I don't want to go.
Time's up, but I really don't want to leave.

usage_en: Anticipate missing something or someone after you leave. Say what you need, then add 이 그리울 것 같아 at the end. Common uses: 한국 음식이 그리울 것 같아. (I think I'll miss Korean food.) or 여기 사람들이 그리울 것 같아. (I think I'll miss the people here.).

examples.en: I think I'll miss Korean food.
I think I'll miss the people here.
I think I'll miss this alley.

usage_en: Make a firm promise to definitely come back to a place. Say what you need, then add 꼭 다시 올게 at the end. Common uses: 너무 좋았어. 꼭 다시 올게. (It was so good. I'll definitely come back.) or 꼭 다시 올게. 약속해. (I'll definitely come back. I promise.).

examples.en: It was so good. I'll definitely come back.
I'll definitely come back. I promise.
I'll definitely come back to Korea.

usage_en: Mark a fluency milestone: thinking directly in Korean without translating. Just place a noun before 이제 한국어로 생각해요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 요즘 이제 한국어로 생각해요. (These days, I now think in Korean.) or 이제 한국어로 생각해요. 번역 안 해도 돼요. (I now think in Korean. I don't need to translate anymore.).

examples.en: These days, I now think in Korean.
I now think in Korean. I don't need to translate anymore.
examples.ko: 이제 한국어로 생각해요. 번역 안 해도 돼요.

examples.en: I now think in Korean. My skills must have improved a lot.
examples.ko: 이제 한국어로 생각해요. 실력이 많이 늘었나봐요.

usage_en: Say you now understand Korean directly without needing to translate. Just place a noun before 번역 안 해도 이해돼요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 이제 번역 안 해도 이해돼요. (Now I understand without translating.) or 한국 드라마 번역 안 해도 이해돼요. (I understand Korean dramas without translating now.).

examples.en: Now I understand without translating.
I understand Korean dramas without translating now.
examples.ko: 한국 드라마 번역 안 해도 이해돼요.

examples.en: I can understand without translating. I feel so good about that.
examples.ko: 번역 안 해도 이해돼요. 기분이 너무 좋아요.

usage_en: Note that someone's ability or skill has grown significantly. Just place a noun before 실력이 많이 늘었어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 한국어 실력이 많이 늘었어요. (My Korean skills have improved a lot.) or 6개월 만에 실력이 많이 늘었어요. (My skills have improved a lot in just 6 months.).

examples.en: My Korean skills have improved a lot.
My skills have improved a lot in just 6 months.
Your skills have improved so much. It's amazing.

usage_en: Reflect that both of you have grown and improved through a shared journey. Say what you need, then add 같이 성장한 것 같아요 at the end. Common uses: 같이 공부하면서 같이 성장한 것 같아요. (Studying together, I feel like we've grown together.) or 우리 같이 성장한 것 같아요. 감사해요. (I feel like we've grown together. Thank you.).

examples.en: Studying together, I feel like we've grown together.
examples.ko: 같이 공부하면서 같이 성장한 것 같아요.

examples.en: I feel like we've grown together. Thank you.
examples.ko: 우리 같이 성장한 것 같아요. 감사해요.

examples.en: It feels like we've grown together. Let's keep going together.
examples.ko: 같이 성장한 것 같아요. 앞으로도 함께해요.

usage_en: Credit someone for helping you learn or grow a lot. Just place a noun before 덕분에 정말 많이 배웠어요 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 여러분 덕분에 정말 많이 배웠어요. (Thanks to all of you, I've learned so much.) or 선생님 덕분에 정말 많이 배웠어요. (Thanks to my teacher, I've really learned a lot.).

examples.en: Thanks to all of you, I've learned so much.
Thanks to my teacher, I've really learned a lot.
Studying together, I've learned so much thanks to you.
examples.ko: 같이 공부해서 덕분에 정말 많이 배웠어요.
